title: Conditional procurement from calibrated demand uncertainty

methodLabels.ML: Approach A: machine learning demand model
methodLabels.Blend: Approach A benchmark: 75% recent matching-slot / 25% previous-week lag blend

explanations.ratio: A shortage:surplus ratio of 4:1 means each missing kWh is assigned 4 hypothetical penalty units, while each extra kWh is assigned 1 unit. It does not describe the amount of electricity or an observed price.
explanations.loss: For a measured interval, penalty = C_under × max(actual demand − purchase, 0) + C_over × max(purchase − actual demand, 0).
explanations.quantileRule: The marginal trade-off is C_under × P(demand > Q) versus C_over × P(demand ≤ Q). Balancing them gives F(Q) = C_under / (C_under + C_over). With 4:1, 4 × 20% = 1 × 80%, so choose P80 under the model distribution.
explanations.P80FullForm: P80 = the 80th percentile of the model-estimated demand distribution. P stands for percentile.
explanations.P80Significance: P80 is a quantity of electricity. In a calibrated model distribution, about 80% of demand outcomes are at or below this quantity and about 20% exceed it. It is not 80% of the point forecast, and it is not a guaranteed probability on future demand.
explanations.whyBuffer: The point forecast is one estimate. Validation prediction errors form an empirical uncertainty distribution around it. The selected percentile of that distribution supplies the purchase buffer. A shortage penalty four times the surplus penalty favours a higher quantity.
explanations.sourceOfUncertainty: These quantiles come from frozen validation residual distributions. ML keeps validation-selected temperature-band conditioning; Blend uses pooled calibration. Full-portfolio quantiles retain a provisional proxy for households without usable target history. No new price model is fitted.
explanations.dailyVsInterval: 14.011 MWh is ML P80 calibrated for the total UTC day. 14.998 MWh is the sum of 96 separately calculated interval P80 purchases. The percentile of a sum generally differs from the sum of percentiles because demand errors are correlated. The latter is not the whole-day P80.
explanations.settlementScope: Daily penalties use net daily demand: surplus at one time can offset shortage at another. Interval penalties score each quarter-hour separately. Choose the objective that matches the settlement rules; these two schedules are not jointly reconciled.
explanations.reduction: The 24.09% figure means the historical interval penalty fell from 1,318,604.24 to 1,000,926.40 hypothetical units compared with purchasing Approach A point forecasts. It is not a percentage reduction in energy purchased or a measured monetary saving.
explanations.comparisonScope: Historical costs use the same retrospectively measured household subset on 34,944 quarter-hours and 364 days. Full-portfolio actual demand was incomplete, so these are not verified costs for all 410 households.
explanations.noActualFinalDay: No actual demand is supplied for 28 February 2024. Its 410-household forecasts and proposed purchases cannot be assigned a verified final-day error or realized saving.
explanations.conditionalRecommendation: For a quarter-hour settlement demonstration with assumed 4:1 penalties, the Approach A P80 interval purchase schedule totals 14.998 MWh against a demand point forecast of 13.015 MWh. This is a conditional policy proposal, not proven real-market optimum.
explanations.optimalityLimits: The rule minimizes expected linear imbalance penalties under the forecast distribution with constant coefficients, no purchase-price term or market constraints. Validation uncertainty is imperfect: ML test P10–P90 coverage is 79.0% by interval and 73.4% by day against nominal 80%. The policy can cost more than the point forecast in some tests, as the 1:1 scenario shows.
explanations.methodDisambiguation: ML and Blend are both Approach A artifacts; Blend is the lag benchmark and is not Approach B Ridge. Scenario letters A–D identify hypothetical penalty cases, not modelling approaches.
explanations.selection: Scenario definitions, quantile rules and calibration were frozen before test policy evaluation. Historical test results did not select or change the policy.
explanations.units: Electricity quantities are kWh per 15-minute interval or MWh per day. Penalties are hypothetical normalized units, not euros; no historical tariff or electricity price data were supplied or inferred.

toyBalance.note: Marginal illustration: at P80, a very small additional purchase has equal expected shortage benefit and surplus cost in a continuous demand distribution. The 100 outcomes are illustrative, not actual observations.
